question: does Authorization: Bearer <aios-operator> reach the AIOS application on the O-A credential hosts?
constraints: read-only; no Production, X2, B3, credential or scope change; no write; neither credential printed or exposed

facts.source: fullstack/backend/api.py, security.py (unchanged since deployed commit d05261c)
facts.finding: B3 reads only the Authorization header; absent, malformed and unknown tokens all yield the same 401 'no authenticated principal'
every bearer request answered by the application (request_id present) with 401; no AIOS_OPERATOR_TOKENS refusal line
Production AIOS_OPERATOR_TOKENS updatedAt 1790837003374, before dpl_76CYC and dpl_s8c6m were built
the operator token matches the recorded sha256 prefix 0ccb723c
same token, same immutable dpl_76CYC, same client code, bypass sent by the client through the same agent proxy: GET /session -> 200, subject aios-operator

facts.source: dummy-header probe to postman-echo.com and httpbin.org (no credential attached)
facts.finding: a placeholder Authorization header arrives unchanged; x-vercel-protection-bypass is not attached to these hosts

only_variable: for the three O-A hosts the bypass is now attached by the environment's API credential instead of being sent by the client
classification: B — the Authorization header does not reach the application intact on the credential hosts (stripped or replaced between client and app)
basis: differential: F3-F5 rule out a token, configuration or deployment cause (C) and a B3 rejection of a correctly received token (A); F6 shows the proxy forwards Authorization on other hosts. Not directly observed at the application, which cannot report whether the header was present (F1)
consequence: D — the provider credential path as configured is incompatible with a client-supplied Authorization header on the same hosts
